ArticleLayout-module-scss-module__W3addq__wrap"><div class="ArticleLayout-module-scss-module__W3addq__content"><div class="text-rich-text text-rich-text--article w-richtext"><p><em><strong>Update</strong>: Auto mode is generally available in Claude Code for all users. (July 10, 2026)</em></p><p>Today, we&#x27;re introducing auto mode, a new permissions mode in Claude Code where Claude makes permission decisions on your behalf, with safeguards monitoring actions before they run. It&#x27;s available now as a research preview on the Team plan, and coming to the Enterprise plan and API users in the coming days.</p><h2 id="how-it-works">How it works</h2><p>Claude Code&#x27;s default permissions are purposefully conservative: every file write and bash command asks for approval. It’s a safe default, but it means you can&#x27;t kick off a large task and walk away, since Claude will request frequent human approvals along the way. While some developers choose to bypass permission checks with --dangerously-skip-permissions, skipping permissions can result in dangerous and destructive outcomes and should not be used outside of isolated environments.</p><p>Auto mode is a middle path that lets you run longer tasks with fewer interruptions while introducing less risk than skipping all permissions. Before each tool call runs, a classifier reviews it to <a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#what-the-classifier-blocks-by-default">check for potentially destructive actions</a> like mass deleting files, sensitive data exfiltration, or malicious code execution.</p><p>Actions that the classifier deems as safe proceed automatically, and risky ones get blocked, redirecting Claude to take a different approach. If Claude insists on taking actions that are continually blocked, it will eventually trigger a permission prompt to the user.</p><h2 id="what-to-expect">What to expect</h2><p>Auto mode reduces risk compared to --dangerously-skip-permissions but doesn&#x27;t eliminate it entirely, and we continue to recommend using it in isolated environments. The classifier may still allow some risky actions: for example, if user intent is ambiguous, or if Claude doesn&#x27;t have enough context about your environment to know an action might create additional risk. It may also occasionally block benign actions. We’ll continue to improve the experience over time.</p><p>Auto mode may have a small impact on token consumption, cost, and latency for tool calls.</p><h2 id="getting-started">Getting started</h2><p>Auto mode is available in Claude Code as a research preview for Claude Team users today, and will roll out to Enterprise and API users in the coming days. It works with both Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6.</p><ul><li><strong>For admins</strong>: Auto mode will soon be available for all Claude Code users on Enterprise, Team, and Claude API plans. To disable it for the CLI and VS Code extension, set &quot;disableAutoMode&quot;: &quot;disable&quot; in your managed settings. Auto mode is disabled by default on the Claude desktop app, and can be toggled on using Organization Settings -&gt; Claude Code.</li><li><strong>For developers</strong>: Run `claude --enable-auto-mode` to enable auto mode, then cycle to it with Shift+Tab. On Desktop and in the VS Code extension, first toggle auto mode on in Settings -&gt; Claude Code, then select it from the permission mode drop-down in a session.</li></ul><p><a href="https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes#eliminate-prompts-with-auto-mode">Explore the docs</a> for more information.</p></div></div></div></div><section
